schema.text: 1:1 permuted-block randomization generated in Stata 14 and performed by the epidemiology and clinical trials unit at ACTREC.

arms.text: Pelvic external-beam radiotherapy 45 to 50 Gy in 23 to 25 fractions over 4.5 to 5 weeks, preferably intensity-modulated photons. Image-guided brachytherapy aims for a cumulative high-risk CTV D90 above 85 Gy EQD2, with 2 cm3 bladder, rectum, sigmoid, and bowel doses not exceeding 90, 75, 75, and 75 Gy EQD2. Treatment is completed within 56 days.

cN0 on pelvic MRI, with no radiographic mesorectal nodal metastasis, tumor deposits, or extramural venous invasion. M0, with no metastatic disease on CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.

publications.title: No operation after short-course radiotherapy followed by consolidation chemotherapy in locally advanced rectal cancer (NOAHS-ARC): study protocol for a prospective, phase II trial.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm multicenter phase II trial (NOAHS-ARC) in Santiago, Chile. Primary endpoint is complete tumor response, combining pathologic complete response and sustained clinical complete response beyond 1 year, compared with a historical 12% rate. Target accrual is 48 evaluable patients. Interim look at 24 patients.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Induction short-course radiotherapy, 25 Gy in five fractions of 5 Gy. Seven to 14 days later, consolidation chemotherapy with either nine cycles of FOLFOX every 14 days (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-fluorouracil bolus 400 mg/m2, and 5-fluorouracil infusion 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours) or six cycles of CAPOX every 21 days (capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 every 12 hours for 14 days and oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1). Response is assessed 4 to 8 weeks after chemotherapy. Clinical complete response may be managed without surgery. Near-complete response is reassessed at 4 weeks. Incomplete response goes to total mesorectal excision.

brief.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Quezada-Diaz et al., International Journal of Colorectal Disease 2025 (PMID 40100473). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Biopsy-proven mismatch-repair-proficient rectal adenocarcinoma, MRI stage II (T3 to 4, N0) or III (any T, N1 or higher), less than 7 cm from the anal verge and palpable. Age over 18. No prior rectal cancer.

Excluded: stage IV, mismatch-repair deficiency, tumor beyond 7 cm or not palpable, exenteration, ECOG above 1, recurrent disease, contraindication to radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or MRI, untreated coronary disease, acute coronary syndrome within 12 months, heart failure, neuropathy, pregnancy or breastfeeding.

Baseline laboratories used for exclusion: hemoglobin under 8 g/dL, white cells under 4000/L as printed, platelets under 100,000/L, creatinine clearance under 50 mL/min. The narrative excludes total bilirubin above 5 mg/dL, while the eligibility table prints the inequality in the opposite direction.
